_comment: Short 2 in docs/CONTENT.md: the January reset. The first line is carried in `variants` because tts.mjs treats that as the hook; here the hook IS the first thing drawn.
_v2: Rewritten 2026-09-17 after a first-time viewer found v1 hard to follow. v1 told November, then January, named the word at 0:35, showed two hospital trips with a bill and EOB each, and split the November visit $100/$300, which quietly raises coinsurance (Short 3's subject). v2 opens on the confusion itself (same visit, $100 then $400), names the word straight away, and shows the bucket once.
_injury: Slipped on ice, which is also why it is January. House style: the injury has to earn its place in the story, not just be different from the last one.
_numbers: A $1,000 deductible and the SAME visit in both months. November says 'insurance paid most of the bill' rather than a split, so the viewer has no arithmetic to do and no second concept to wonder about.

variants.ice: Your body does not know it is January. Your insurance does.

body.text: In November, this visit cost you a hundred dollars. Today it costs four hundred.
Same visit. The bill is not wrong.
It is your deductible. What you pay yourself each year, before insurance starts helping.
Picture a bucket. Yours holds a thousand dollars.
By November you had filled it, so insurance paid most of the bill.
So you pay the whole bill yourself again, until it fills back up.
Check yours before you dispute. Or upload your bill free at UseClaimRight.com.
